correctness.rationale: The exact identity Q^4=-I+3B makes the normalized multiple-of-four Fibonacci term equal to 1+3(u-1)(u-2) modulo 9; for j>=4 the binomial-series coefficient 3^(j-1)/j has 3-adic valuation at least 2. Nonmultiple terms follow by Q^(4u+r)=(-1)^u(I-3uB)Q^r modulo 9. Four-index blocks yield the exact 3-adic unit product 2^m 7^floor(m/3) u_3(m!) R_m(r); the factorial valuation is m+v3(m!). Combining quotient valuation and unit separately gives 3^delta 2^delta 7^eta W m!/(a!b!). In the delta=0 case, eta=1 forces a ternary carry and 3|binom(m,a), so 7^eta can be dropped modulo 9; in delta=1 the factor 6 makes it drop. Direct exact Fibotorial integer division checks 13,041 pairs in all rows through 160; finite computation is not used as proof.

originality.rationale: Unlike prior exact signed prime-modulus congruences (2018) and parity/fractal results (2013), the claim describes every Fibonomial residue modulo 9. The 2018 result is a reduction modulo 3 of the present result and cannot distinguish residues separated by 3. The 2025 all-valuation matrix theorem computes 3-adic orders but not unit residues modulo 9, so it cannot imply the claimed congruence. No full modulo-nine equivalent was located by targeted searches, but prior unlocated literature is a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated specialized formula for Fibonacci-binomial coefficients modulo nine might be equivalent under a different notation.

value.rationale: This is a complete arithmetic refinement from prime to first prime-square modulus for the natural Fibonomial triangle. It distinguishes all nonzero 3-adic unit residues and the valuation-one case, where all information vanishes on reducing modulo 3. It gives every index pair via one ordinary binomial coefficient and four tiny units, with a structural four-block unit-factor lemma and separate exact base-four carry cases. The object and invariant are motivated by the previously studied mod-three Fibonomial fractal and signed Lucas laws; it is not an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
